title: Signal reduction for paging + automated on-call actions for multi-region failover
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Objective: Reduce noisy pages and hard-to-triage alerts while automating safe on-call actions for multi-region failover and circuit-breaker-triggered load shedding. This ticket covers alert tuning (signal-to-noise improvement), on-call runbook creation for region degraded scenarios, and automation scaffolding to perform pre-approved mitigations (traffic draining, circuit breaker toggles, limited failover) with guardrails tied to SLO thresholds. Scope excludes re-architecting the routing layer itself (separate initiative) but includes webhooks and scripted run-of-play automation in the ops repo.
acceptance_criteria: 1) PagerDuty paging rate for SEV3/SEV2 reduced by >=60% without increasing time-to-detect for SEV0/SEV1. 2) Documented runbooks for 'Region partial outage' and 'KV cache thrash' with clear next steps and escalation points in Confluence. 3) Automated failover playbook (dry-run) that: a) flips traffic routing in the staging project, b) exercises circuit-breaker rollback, c) sends structured incident summary to on-call Slack + PagerDuty. 4) New synthetic checks and SLO-aligned alert thresholds deployed to prod with a one-week observation window and rollback plan. 5) Post-rollout alert noise measured and reported with before/after metrics.
proposal:
- Replace several token-level latency alerts that fire on single-instance outliers with aggregated-quantile alerts (p95/p99 by prod-route) and session-aware slow-start detection.
- Add a two-stage paging policy: SEV0/1 immediate page; SEV2 page only after correlated signals (error rate + host-level OOM/GC or increased queue depth); SEV3 -> Slack-only triage.
- Implement an automated playbook runner (ops/playbooks/auto-failover) that executes pre-authorized steps when SLO breach conditions are met for X minutes, with a manual confirmation window for all non-safe operations.
- Instrument circuit-breakers to emit structured events to the incident bus; allow runbook to flip breaker to 'restricted' (percent-based shedding) as intermediate step before full region failover.
- Add smoke-safeguards: canary traffic shift, health check roll-forward, automatic rollback on error spike.
design_decisions: Use quantile-based alerts (p95/p99) instead of mean/avg to avoid noisy CPU bursts triggering pages.
Correlate service-level error spikes with infra signals (host OOM, GPU queue length) before paging.
Expose circuit-breaker state and recent shed fraction in dashboards for faster triage.
Automation must require a one-click confirmation from on-call (configurable) for production failovers unless a safety threshold (SLO breach >30m and global region health degraded) is met.
Prefer Slack + structured message threads for low-severity signals; reserve PagerDuty escalations for verified multi-signal incidents.
runbooks: Region partial outage - steps: 1) Confirm synthetic check failures across >=2 AZs in region; 2) Check circuit-breaker events for widespread shedding; 3) If safe, trigger traffic drain for impacted pool, promote standby pool in secondary region, verify canaries; 4) If canary passes, promote full failover and notify customer-facing channels; 5) Post-incident RCA template link: https://confluence.redwood/reliability/rca-template

KV cache thrash - steps: 1) Check KV hit rates and eviction counts, 2) Toggle cache-size soft-limit to reduce eviction churn, 3) Switch read-path to cached-fallback or reduce QPS by applying percent-based shedding, 4) Monitor error rates for 15m before paging to SEV2/1
automation_tasks: Webhook integration with PagerDuty and Slack with structured runbook events
CI test harness to run dry-run failover in staging every 24h to validate automation and canary checks
Metric rollups and dashboard panels showing pre/post failover latency, error rate, and shed fraction
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for playbook runner and circuit-breaker toggles.
- Staging full dry-run failover executed by SRE team with post-test checklist.
- Gradual prod rollout: alert threshold change + synthetic checks for 48h; enable automated dry-run (no write actions) for 24h; enable manual-confirm automations for 1 week; enable conditional auto-actions for long-lived SLO breaches.
- Post-deploy: measure pager rate and mean-time-to-detect for 7 days and compare to baseline.
